--- title: "Data Exploration and Limitations" subtitle: "GFW vessel presence and apparent fishing effort, Ørsted AOI 2016–2026" --- ## What these data are Two response variables, both pulled from the Global Fishing Watch 4Wings API via `gfwr` v3.0 and both constrained to the Ørsted area of interest — the dissolved union of the South Fork Wind, Revolution Wind and Sunrise Wind 10 km buffers. | | Vessel presence | Apparent fishing effort | |---|---|---| | `gfwr` call | `gfw_ais_presence()` | `gfw_ais_fishing_hours()` | | Measure | Count of hours with ≥1 AIS position | Hours classified as fishing by GFW's behavioural model | | Grain | vessel × 0.01° cell × day | vessel × 0.01° cell × day | | Units | integer, 1–24 | continuous, 0–25.3 | Both were pulled at `spatial_resolution="HIGH"` (0.01°, ~1 km), `temporal_resolution="DAILY"`, `group_by="VESSEL_ID"`, `region_source="USER_SHAPEFILE"`, across eleven calendar-year calls (`gfw_vp_afe_dataPull_090126.Rmd:88-195, 262-369`). No `filter_by` was applied at the API, so no flag, gear or confidence filtering happened server-side. **These are not the same measure.** Presence is an hour *count*; effort is an integrated *duration*. Do not ratio one against the other without saying so. ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import warnings, logging warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") logging.basicConfig(level=logging.ERROR) import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd from gfw_fishing_osw_ais import config as cfg, explore, io, transitions as tr pd.set_option("display.width", 200) ``` ::: ## Development stages Stage boundaries were assigned in the R pull and carried through as a `Development Stage` column. They are near-balanced in length, which is what makes a three-way comparison viable. ::: {#tbl-stages .cell tbl-cap='Development stage definitions' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} pd.DataFrame([ {"Stage": s.label, "Start": s.start, "End": s.end, "Months": s.n_months, "Rationale": s.description} for s in cfg.STAGES.values() ]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

2 Stage 3 2023-04-01 2026-07-01 40 Construction and operation; seabed prep for SF...
``` ::: ::: ## Gear classification `Gear Type` is a fixed per-vessel registry attribute — no vessel in the dataset carries more than one label — so classification is a lookup, not an inference. `POLE_AND_LINE` is kept separate rather than folded into mobile gear. Commercial pole-and-line is not a Southern New England fishery, and the vessel names in that class (MISTE ROSE, FISHIN ADDICTION 17, TUF GUY, TRANQUILITY, PREVAIL) indicate recreational and for-hire charter vessels carrying AIS. `UNRESOLVED` collects `FISHING`, `INCONCLUSIVE` and missing labels — fishing vessels whose gear GFW did not determine. It is carried through the analysis as a reported class rather than dropped, because its growth across stages is a finding in its own right (@sec-degradation). ::: {#tbl-gear .cell tbl-cap='Gear classes and their constituent GFW labels' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = [] for cls in cfg.ANALYSIS_GEAR_CLASSES + (cfg.EXCLUDED,): labels = sorted(k for k, v in cfg.GEAR_CLASS_MAP.items() if v == cls) rows.append({"Class": cls, "GFW Gear Type values": ", ".join(labels)}) pd.DataFrame(rows) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

This is a change in registry coverage, not in fleet behaviour, and it means any gear-stratified comparison across stages is partly measuring GFW's metadata rather than the fishery. ::: {#cell-fig-degradation .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} pivot = comp_afe.pivot(index="stage", columns="gear_class", values="pct_stage_hours") pivot = pivot[list(cfg.ANALYSIS_GEAR_CLASSES)] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2)) bottom = np.zeros(len(pivot)) colors = {"MOBILE": "#b2182b", "FIXED": "#2166ac", "POLE_AND_LINE": "#f4a582", "UNRESOLVED": "#999999"} for col in pivot.columns: ax.bar([cfg.STAGES[s].label for s in pivot.index], pivot[col], bottom=bottom, label=col.replace("_", " ").title(), color=colors[col]) bottom += pivot[col].to_numpy() ax.set_ylabel("% of stage apparent fishing hours") ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=4, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.08)) ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False) plt.tight_layout() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Share of apparent fishing hours by gear class across stages. The unresolved share more than doubles into Stage 3.](01-data-exploration_files/figure-html/fig-degradation-output-1.png){#fig-degradation width=1264 height=657} ::: ::: ## Distribution of the analysis variable The spatial statistics run on per-cell monthly mean hours. That variable is heavily right-skewed and structurally zero-inflated: `MonthMean` divides by the *whole stage length*, so a cell inactive for the entire stage is an exact zero. ::: {#tbl-distribution .cell tbl-cap='Per-cell distribution diagnostics, apparent fishing effort' execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} explore.distribution_diagnostics("afe") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}

This confirms the choice made in the archived ArcGIS workflow and extends it to the gear-stratified surfaces, which had not previously been checked. Neither transform fully normalises the variable — the spike at exactly zero does not move under any monotonic transform — but sqrt gets furthest. The raw field is retained throughout as a sensitivity check. ## Limitations Each of these is a measured quantity, not an adjective. ::: {#tbl-limitations .cell tbl-cap='Quantified dataset limitations' execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} pd.concat([explore.limitations("vp"), explore.limitations("afe")]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}

Stage % of records at modal hour value

``` ::: ::: Between 94% and 98% of vessel-presence records sit at the modal value of one hour. The variable counts hours in which a vessel had at least one AIS position, so it is a discrete count with a hard floor, not a continuous duration. Any distributional model would need a one-inflated or hurdle treatment. Apparent fishing effort does not share this property. ### AIS coverage grows over the study period ::: {#tbl-rates .cell tbl-cap='Effort normalised by stage length and by vessel count' execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} rates = tr.stage_rates("afe") rates.query("gear_class in ['ALL', 'MOBILE', 'FIXED']") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Absolute hours are not comparable across stages on their own. Reporting hours per month alongside hours per vessel-month separates the two explanations: if hours per month rises while hours per vessel-month is flat, the increase is fleet coverage rather than intensified activity. For mobile gear, hours per vessel-month is 1\.28 → 1\.56 → 1\.20 — it rises then returns below baseline. For fixed gear it is 1\.03 → 0\.87 → 1\.78, a genuine intensification on top of a growing fleet. ### Other caveats - **Apparent fishing effort carries a `> 0.32` hour threshold** (`Rmd:531-535`); vessel presence does not. The two datasets are filtered differently. - **Ørsted charter vessels are removed for Stages 2–3 only**, retaining their pre-construction records as genuine fishing. This is deliberate but asymmetric, and must be stated for any before/after reading. Eleven vessels beyond the 35 on Ørsted's own list were identified during this analysis, each with its scope and confidence recorded in `references/vessel_removals.csv` — see `00b-plan-revisions.qmd`. - **`Vessel ID` is not a stable hull identifier.** The 4Wings `group_by="VESSEL_ID"` returns identity *segments*: 1,258 MMSIs map to more than one Vessel ID, up to five. The inflation is stage-dependent, so counting Vessel IDs would manufacture a spurious decline. MMSI is used throughout. ::: {#tbl-identity .cell tbl-cap='Vessel ID inflation relative to MMSI, by stage' execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} explore.vessel_identity_inflation("vp") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ```{=html}

1 vp 2 953 755 1.262
2 vp 3 956 836 1.144
``` ::: ::: - **Stage 3's final month is partial** — data ends 2026-07-13. - **Structural zeros are not missing data.** 107–212 cells (vessel presence) and roughly 1,100–1,900 cells (apparent fishing effort) are exact zeros because the monthly mean divides by the full stage length. ## Reproducing the source data The CSVs this document reads are gitignored. To regenerate them, run `r/scripts/rmd/gfw_vp_afe_dataPull_090126.Rmd` with a valid `GFW_TOKEN`. The vessel removals it applies are read from `references/vessel_removals.csv`, which is tracked, and are matched on **MMSI** rather than `Vessel Name` — a name match cannot reliably remove a vessel, because one hull emits several name strings. The script validates that file on load and stops if it is malformed. Python reads the same file, so the two cannot drift apart.
